title: Which values can the missing eleventh value be?
description: Ten values are known and an eleventh value p is missing. The median of all eleven must be twenty nine, which is the sixth value when sorted. Testing where p lands in the sorted list shows which of the seven choices work.
teaching_notes: One idea: the median of eleven values is the sixth sorted value, so a missing value must not push the known twenty nine out of sixth place. Watch for students who test only the choices one at a time without sorting.

source: Figure it Out (mean and median, question 9)
video_script.why: A child who has found a median by sorting now decides where a missing value may sit so that the median stays fixed.
video_script.substitution: the book's ten known values, the missing value p and the median 29
video_script.anchor: a sorted row of the ten known values with a gap for p
video_script.payoff_line: The value can be forty, one hundred, twenty nine, forty seven or thirty

final_answer.spoken: the value can be forty, one hundred, twenty nine, forty seven or thirty

never_show: 10 or 25 marked as a possible value of p
maths_rules: with p there are 11 values, so the median is the 6th sorted value
if p is at least 29, the six smallest values are 8, 8, 12, 18, 25, 29, so the 6th is 29
if p is less than 29, the six smallest values include p and the 6th is less than 29 (25 when p is at most 25, and p when p is between 25 and 29)
10 and 25 are less than 29, so they fail; 40, 100, 29, 47 and 30 are at least 29, so they work
check: p = 30 gives 8, 8, 12, 18, 25, 29, 30, ... with 6th value 29; p = 25 gives 8, 8, 12, 18, 25, 25, 29, ... with 6th value 25
video_script.design: One sorted row all video. Each choice for p drops into the row, and the sixth place is watched to see whether it stays at twenty nine.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the ten values 12, 47, 8, 73, 18, 35, 39, 8, 29, 25 and a box marked p; the words median 29

marks.book: the title card From your book appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the median.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten values are known. Twelve, forty seven, eight, seventy three, eighteen, thirty five, thirty nine, eight, twenty nine, twenty five.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>An eleventh value is not known, and the median of all eleven must be twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='choices'/>Which of these can the eleventh value be? Ten, twenty five, forty, one hundred, twenty nine, forty seven, thirty.

beats.on_screen: the row, the gap and the choices stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: 11 sorted values: five below the middle, the 6th is the median, five above

marks.eleven: a row of eleven sorted dots appears
marks.six: the 6th dot is marked as the median with five dots on each side

narration: <bookmark mark='eleven'/>With eleven values, the median is the sixth value when they are sorted.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Five values lie below it and five lie above it.

marks.given: the ten known values, the box p and the median are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, ten values are known, one value is missing, and the median of all eleven is twenty nine.

beats.on_screen: To find: which choices can be p

marks.find: the words which choices can be p are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which choices can be the missing value.

marks.sort: the ten known values slide into sorted order

narration: <bookmark mark='sort'/>Step one, sort the ten known values. Eight, eight, twelve, eighteen, twenty five, twenty nine, thirty five, thirty nine, forty seven, seventy three.
<bookmark mark='six'/>The sixth of these ten values is twenty nine.

beats.on_screen: p at least 29: p goes at or after 29, so the 6th value stays 29

marks.high: p drops in at or after the 29 and the 6th place stays 29

narration: <bookmark mark='high'/>Step two, try a missing value that is twenty nine or more. It goes beside the twenty nine or after it, so the sixth value stays twenty nine.

beats.on_screen: p less than 29: p goes before 29, so the 6th value is less than 29

marks.low: p drops in before the 29 and 29 slides to 7th place
marks.less: the 6th place now holds a value less than 29

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step three, try a missing value below twenty nine. It goes before the twenty nine and pushes it to seventh place.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Then the sixth value is below twenty nine, and the median is not twenty nine.

beats.on_screen: sort the choices: below 29: 10, 25 (no); 29 or more: 40, 100, 29, 47, 30 (yes)

marks.no: 10 and 25 are crossed out as below 29
marks.yes: 40, 100, 29, 47 and 30 get ticks as 29 or more

narration: <bookmark mark='no'/>Step four, sort the choices. Ten and twenty five are below twenty nine, so they fail.
<bookmark mark='yes'/>Forty, one hundred, twenty nine, forty seven and thirty are twenty nine or more, so they work.

beats.on_screen: check: p = 30 gives 8, 8, 12, 18, 25, 29, 30, ... with 6th value 29; p = 25 gives 8, 8, 12, 18, 25, 25, 29, ... with 6th value 25

marks.pass: thirty is placed in the row and the 6th dot reads 29
marks.fail: twenty five is placed in the row and the 6th dot reads 25

narration: <bookmark mark='pass'/>Check one choice that works and one that fails. With thirty, the sixth value is still twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='fail'/>With twenty five, the row has two twenty fives. The sixth value is twenty five, not twenty nine.

marks.ans: the five working choices are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The value can be forty, one hundred, twenty nine, forty seven or thirty.
